cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold my spare cupboard key until tomorrow. Don't mention it to your flatmate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll label it so she doesn't mistake it for ours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No label. Identifying a key for someone who mustn't know it's here defeats the arrangement. Keep it in your purse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm lending her the purse tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put it in your own coat. Check the pockets before you lend anyone anything else.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects B2's labeling idea as a confidentiality error. B4's purse loan then makes A5 supervise belongings while retaining B as custodian of an unexplained key.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 proposes avoiding key confusion, which A3 converts into a concealment issue. B4 removes the purse as a secure place; A5 names a personal alternative and a check before lending.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants orderly storage and B4 discloses a planned loan. Neither reply requires B to know the purpose of the secret.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4's ordinary purse loan into a broader check on B's handling, increasing A's strained management without escalating the secret itself.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard key, flatmate and tomorrow deadline define the favor. B4 specifies tonight's purse loan, explaining why A5 must change location.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's full explanation is slightly formal but aims to stop labeling; A5's pocket check has a concrete recipient and purpose.
